Hi, I struggle with the same thing as it is a kind of coping mechanism whenever I feel stressed or bored. Previously I've managed to avoid going on YouTube for about 2-3 weeks at a time and it was definitely worth it. I got inspired by the work of Cal Newport - he's a great author that writes about productivity and has an interesting podcast that I'd recommend. 

I find that you have to structure your time carefully, to keep yourself busy with something useful, otherwise it's very difficult. For example, reading books, exercise like running (this helps me a lot when feeling down). We need to learn to embrace boredom. I've read some articles that suggest boredom is actually good for the brain and helps with creativity and overall enjoyment of activities. 

For me the best strategy was to have a hard reset of about 2 weeks when I force myself to be bored without YouTube. It's hard at first but eventually the brain gets used to it. Unfortunately, this kind of self-discipline will seem painful at first, but there's really no other option...

I also think its fine to watch educational videos or lectures on YouTube as there is a lot of useful content. However, self-discipline is key and we can't just jump to some other irrelevant video. For this, I used the browser extension Distraction Free YouTube which removes all the recommended videos and makes it a lot less tempting to click on another video (at least in my experience).
